title: The Shinto Shrine Torii's Surprising Code
notes: Detective-cast subplot (Conan/Shin'ichi, Ai Haibara, Agasa, and the Detective Boys Ayumi/Mitsuhiko/Genta) omitted by convention -- their beetle-hunting/secret-code game runs in parallel and shares a thematic trick (mirror/backward reading) with the real dying message, but never intersects the murder's evidence graph. Ran Mouri and Sonoko Suzuki are kept as full person nodes despite being series regulars because they are directly targeted: Sonoko's bag/phone is stolen to suppress photographic evidence, and both are driven off-route and menaced by the culprit in his car. No `event` node type: every action is a directly typed edge between the entities involved. The old lower-fidelity case file (cases/ep411-412...) lists an 'attempted attack with a knife' in the forest -- the transcript shows no knife; the actual attempted attack is Kano driving Ran and Sonoko off-route in his car to interrogate them about Shin'ichi's whereabouts, ended when Ran kicks him and the car crashes into a tree. The old file also omits Bito and Yanuma's names/roles and the blackmail motive entirely, and mislabels the dying message's true content (it renders as the culprit's own name, 'Kano', when the sideways scrawl is flipped/mirrored -- the same backward-reading trick that solves the Detective Boys' separate 'marumushi ni tento' -> 'muramatsuri no torii' puzzle). case_type: murder.

clues.desc: Window scrawl read normally looks like 'teiu'/'TEL shite'; turned sideways and mirror-flipped -- the same trick that turns the kids' 'marumushi ni tento' into 'muramatsuri no torii' -- it spells 'Kano'.
Calling back the number that texted about the 'found' bag makes a phone ring inside Kano's own pocket, proving he is holding Sonoko's stolen phone.
